<!-- plain-summary -->
This is a decision about listing a directory: today the production store loads all of a directory's entries into memory at once, so a directory with very many files could use a lot of memory. It matters as a memory-cost tradeoff, and it should be settled by measuring real directory sizes — because the alternative, fetching entries in pages, would require changing the shared storage interface that both backends must implement.

**Open question (M4).** `scan` returns a materialized `Vec`, so a directory with very many dirents buffers fully in memory. Whether M4 accepts this, or a later **trait evolution** adds a paginated/streaming scan, is a **measurement** question — and a trait change is explicitly **out of M4's "unchanged trait" scope** (the milestone's whole premise). Decide by measurement, not now.

**To resolve**
- [ ] measure memory cost of large-directory `scan` buffering at realistic dirent counts
- [ ] decide whether buffering is acceptable for M4 (it is, by default — the trait stays unchanged)
- [ ] if not, scope a **post-M4** paginated/streaming `scan` trait evolution (both backends to carry)

**Refs:** proposal 0007 §Open questions ("Large-directory `scan` buffering"), §"Alternatives considered" (paginated/streaming scan deferred). Related: #254 (M4.3).

comments.body: **Cross-reference from #261 (read consistency):** the decided level pins **one snapshot timestamp across all internal pages of a single `scan()` call** (a consistent cut) for the M4 materialized scan. If this issue's resolution later evolves the trait toward a **paginated/streaming scan**, the consistency question **re-opens at the trait level**: per-page snapshots would let a concurrent rename appear in zero or two pages of one logical listing — so any streaming design must either hold one snapshot across the stream (TiKV snapshot lifetime/GC-safepoint implications) or explicitly document the weaker cut. Decision + rationale: https://github.com/getwyrd/wyrd/issues/261#issuecomment-4871148134

## Plan and recommendation (2026-07-03; governed by proposal 0015, which promoted this to a known limitation with an interim paging cap)

### What the research established

**1. Two distinct consumer classes, and the issue names the smaller one.** (a) **Directory listing** (`dirent:<parent>/` prefixes) — scales with directory shape; the nominal case. (b) **Custodian full-store scans** — GC, reconstruction, rebalance, and backfill each scan the *entire* `inode:` prefix every reconcile pass (plus the `pending:`/`repair:` ledgers). Class (b) scales with total object count, not directory fan-out, and is the real unbounded-growth driver on the network backend.

**2. A correctness constraint stronger than memory: the cap MUST be fail-loud.** GC builds its never-reclaim safety set from the `inode:` scan — a **silently truncated scan is not a performance bug, it is data loss** (a referenced fragment missing from the set becomes reclaimable). So whatever the interim paging cap does on breach, it must be `Err` with an operator-visible signal — **never truncation**. This is the one non-negotiable this plan adds to #254's implementation.

**3. #261's decided consistency binds any evolution.** One snapshot per `scan()` (consistent cut) is decided; a future paginated/streaming trait re-opens per-page semantics *and* adds a TiKV constraint — a long-lived stream's snapshot can outlive the GC safepoint.

**4. The trait stays unchanged in M4** — the milestone's premise; the issue already says decide-by-measurement.

### Recommendation

- **M4 (as specced + the constraint above):** materialized `Vec`, internal paging per #254, interim cap breach = fail-loud `Err` + audit signal, sized well above expected counts. The trait is untouched.
- **Measurement (checkbox 1):** a large-directory + large-store leg piggybacked on the #257 Tier-1/Tier-2 campaign — bytes/entry at realistic dirent counts *and* full-store `inode:` scan cost at realistic object counts (class (b) is the number that matters).
- **Post-M4 evolution — two different shapes for the two classes, neither built speculatively:**
  - *Directories* want **paginated listing** — and the natural forcing function is #364's S3 `ListObjectsV2` pagination (pre-M8), which imposes exactly this shape at the gateway. Design the trait evolution there, when it is forced, with per-page snapshot semantics documented (per #261's cross-reference).
  - *Custodians* want **resumable cursor passes** (checkpointed reconcile position), not a streaming trait — they already tolerate staleness between passes; cursoring the pass keeps the trait narrow.
- **Named triggers for re-opening (deferred ≠ forgotten):** measurement shows the envelope breached at target scale, **or** #364's ListObjectsV2 lands — whichever first. This issue stays open until the measurement lands, then closes with the numbers recorded; the evolution issue is filed *then*, not now.

**Refs:** proposal 0015 §Open questions / known-limitation note; #254 (M4.3 — hosts the cap; fail-loud constraint attached there); #261 (consistency cut); #257 (measurement leg); #364 (the pagination forcing function); ADR-0011 (the audit signal).

milestone.title: M4 — Production metadata backend
milestone.description: Step 2. Swap embedded redb for distributed TiKV behind the unchanged MetadataStore trait; multi-key atomic directory ops hold under the distributed store. Completes the single-zone data plane — a soft stopping point, not the release: the ★ Step-2 release point is M8 (proposal 0013 implementation arc, supersedes 0002). Plan: proposal 0015 (supersedes 0007; acceptance PR #417); tracker #201; first-deployment gate #367.

title: M4 open question — large-directory scan buffering (materialized Vec) vs later paginated/streaming trait evolution

resolved.note: Resolved outside a PDCA cycle — the open question was decided in the GitHub issue comments; this bundle is a notes-only tracker, not a result bundle (no brief/patch/SUMMARY). Marked 2026-07-18.
